findings.practical_consequence: A planner cannot implement or prove worktree-safe interception because the package names a launcher-owned per-session configuration and an authentication constraint without grounding the configuration installation mechanism, capability-proof route, or authorized authentication route that the launcher must use.

A planner cannot make the registered-use denominator reproducible because the claimed READY obligation requires a finite recurrence-and-availability policy but supplies neither its exact immutable decision inputs nor a grounded owner and route for providing them before the controller records eligibility.

A planner would treat all but four owners as source-grounded even though the authoritative descriptor records six owners requiring custodian evidence; it therefore cannot produce a complete fail-closed 25-owner contract or its all-owner verification without rediscovering missing evidence.
